heading.zh: 统计概率与连胜的不可思议性
heading.en: Statistical Improbability of a Winning Streak

paragraphs.zh: 萨曼莎·麦克勒莫尔在文章中指出，比尔·米勒连续十五年（1991-2005）跑赢标普500指数的表现具有惊人的统计概率上的不可能性，她引用前同事迈克尔·莫布索因的计算结果，即如果仅凭运气而非技能实现这一壮举的概率仅为二百三十万分之一，并强调尽管有人质疑这是纯粹的运气，但正如斯蒂芬·杰伊·古尔德所言，长连胜总是技能与运气的结合。
paragraphs.en: Samantha McLemore argues in her article that Bill Miller's performance of outperforming the S&P 500 Index for fifteen consecutive years (1991-2005) is statistically improbable, citing a calculation by former colleague Michael Mauboussin which states that the odds of achieving this streak purely by luck are one in 2.3 million, and she emphasizes that while some contend it was pure luck, as noted by Stephen Jay Gould, long winning streaks are always a combination of skill and luck.

heading.zh: 跨策略与全周期的业绩表现
heading.en: Performance Across Strategies and Full Market Cycles

paragraphs.zh: 萨曼莎·麦克勒莫尔在《A Look at Bill's Record》中论证了比尔·米勒的业绩不仅具有统计上的显著性，而且跨越了多种策略和完整的市场周期。她指出，在所有四种投资策略中，米勒在 68% 的年份里跑赢了市场，这一比例远高于共同基金平均仅 38% 的胜率，甚至超过了那些拥有连胜记录的最佳基金的 55% 胜率 [s2]。为了证明其长期回报的卓越性，她引用了具体数据：在管理价值权益策略期间，米勒每年净收益为 12.39%，而标普 500 指数为 11.09%，投资者若投入 1 万美元，最终将获得 321,461 美元而非指数的 227,576 美元，额外增值超过 93,000 美元（增幅 41%）[s2]。此外，在机会权益策略中，米勒每年净收益为 7.35%，远超标普 500 的 4.19%，尽管该时期市场整体回报较低，但米勒仍实现了比指数高 75% 的年化超额收益，使 1 万美元的投资最终多出 11,056 美元（增幅 58%）[s2]。麦克勒莫尔进一步强调，这些事实背后的关键是人本身：尽管米勒拥有名声、财富和成功，但他并未选择转向“隐形指数化”策略以保留稳定的管理费流，而是坚持追求最佳回报，这体现了他作为真正善良之人的品格 [s4]。
paragraphs.en: In 'A Look at Bill's Record', Samantha McLemore argues that Bill Miller's performance is not only statistically significant but also spans multiple strategies and full market cycles. She points out that across all four investment strategies, Miller beat the market in 68% of the years, a rate significantly higher than the average mutual fund's 38% win rate and even exceeding the 55% achieved by the best funds with winning streaks [s2]. To demonstrate the excellence of his long-term returns, she cites specific data: during his tenure managing the Value Equity strategy, Miller generated an annual net return of 12.39% versus the S&P 500's 11.09%, meaning an investor who put in $10,000 would have ended with $321,461 compared to the index's $227,576, resulting in an additional gain of over $93,000 (a 41% increase) [s2]. Furthermore, in the Opportunity Equity strategy, Miller achieved an annual net return of 7.35%, far surpassing the S&P 500's 4.19%; despite this being a period of lower overall market returns, Miller still delivered an annual outperformance 75% higher than the index, turning $10,000 into an additional $11,056 (a 58% increase) [s2]. McLemore further emphasizes that the key behind these facts is the person himself: despite his fame, fortune, and success, he did not choose to switch to a 'closet-indexing' strategy to preserve a steady fee stream, but instead persisted in pursuing the best possible returns, reflecting his character as a genuinely good person [s4].

heading.zh: 逆境中的表现与危机应对
heading.en: Performance in Downturns and Crisis Response

paragraphs.zh: 萨曼莎·麦克勒莫尔在文章中驳斥了比尔·格罗斯仅擅长牛市而忽视危机的指控，指出其管理的四种策略（价值股权、机会股权、乐嘉马逊小盘股及收入机会）在所有四个策略中均跑赢了各自基准指数，且在所有策略的 12 个下行年份中有 8 年（67%）实现了超额收益。她引用了格罗斯承认 2008 年金融危机是“一个极其巨大的错误”这一事实，强调该错误的规模之大而非数量之少，以此证明其业绩记录在逆境中依然扎实，并反驳了记者关于他“只有一个错误”的评论。
paragraphs.en: Samantha McLemore refutes the accusation that Bill Gross excels only in bull markets while ignoring crises, noting that his four managed strategies (Value Equity, Opportunity Equity, Legg Mason Small Cap, and Income Opportunity) all outperformed their respective benchmark indices. She cites Gross's admission that the 2008 financial crisis was "a REALLY BIG mistake," emphasizing the magnitude of the error rather than its singularity, to demonstrate that his track record remains solid in down markets and to counter the reporter's comment about him having "one mistake."

heading.zh: 能力与品格的区分及行业选择
heading.en: Distinguishing Skill from Character and Industry Choice

paragraphs.zh: 萨曼莎·麦克勒莫尔在讨论比尔·米勒的长期投资业绩时，明确区分了‘能力’与‘品格’两个维度：她承认米勒拥有令人难以置信的投资天赋和持续十五年的超额回报记录，但更强调其作为人的道德品质——即在巨大财富、名声和成功之后，依然坚持做正确的事，拒绝转向能带来稳定费流但会导致投资者长期跑输市场的‘隐形指数化策略’。她的论证逻辑是：真正的伟大不仅在于技术上的卓越（如他面对任何话题都能提供有趣见解、不断适应改进、敢于承认错误），更在于这种卓越背后的道德坚守；她以米勒在十五连胜后本可选择却未选择降低风险换取稳定收益的具体行为为例，证明其品格优于单纯的能力，并指出尽管存在个人偏见，但米勒已无可辩驳地证明了自身作为伟大投资者的资格。
paragraphs.en: Samantha McLemore distinguishes between 'skill' and 'character' when discussing Bill Miller's long-term investment performance: she acknowledges his extraordinary investment talent and the remarkable fifteen-year streak of outperformance, but emphasizes his moral character—specifically, that despite immense wealth, fame, and success, he continues to do the right thing by refusing to switch to a 'closet-indexing strategy' that would provide stable fee streams at the cost of consistent underperformance for investors. Her reasoning is that true greatness lies not only in technical excellence (such as his ability to offer interesting insights on any topic, his constant adaptation and improvement, and his willingness to admit mistakes) but also in the moral integrity behind it; she illustrates this with the specific example of Miller choosing not to lower risk for stability after his fifteen-year winning streak, arguing that while her perspective is admittedly biased, Bill Miller has undeniably proven himself as a great investor.
